probes.query: Where is the suspend function `coroutineScope` defined that creates a new scope and only returns once all of its child coroutines have completed?
expectedFacts: coroutineScope is declared as `public suspend fun <R> coroutineScope(block: suspend CoroutineScope.() -> R): R` and is implemented via suspendCoroutineUninterceptedOrReturn creating a ScopeCoroutine that calls startUndispatchedOrReturn
probes.author: kotlin-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'public suspend fun <R> coroutineScope' kotlinx-coroutines-core/common/src/CoroutineScope.kt -> CoroutineScope.kt:842. Body (lines 842-850) uses suspendCoroutineUninterceptedOrReturn + ScopeCoroutine + startUndispatchedOrReturn. Note the unrelated `public fun CoroutineScope(context: CoroutineContext)` factory lower in the same file is a different symbol; query anchors on 'suspend function' + 'waits for children'.

probes.query: Find the actual implementation of the CoroutineScope.launch coroutine builder — the real one that constructs a StandaloneCoroutine, not the deprecated overloads.
expectedFacts: The real CoroutineScope.launch (in Builders.common.kt) takes context, start and a suspend block, builds newCoroutineContext(context), then creates a LazyStandaloneCoroutine if start.isLazy else a StandaloneCoroutine, and returns it as a Job after calling coroutine.start
probes.author: kotlin-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'public fun CoroutineScope.launch' across common/src returns Builders.common.kt:200 (REAL impl, body constructs StandaloneCoroutine/LazyStandaloneCoroutine) AND Guidance.kt:184 & Guidance.kt:251 which are `@Deprecated(...)` overloads that just delegate (`launch(context as CoroutineContext, start, block)`). HARD: 3 functions share the exact name 'launch'; the gold is the one with the constructing body, the two in Guidance.kt are deprecation shims a naive symbol/definition lookup is likely to surface first.

probes.query: Which Flow operator keeps only emissions that are instances of a generic type parameter, using a reified type? Find its definition.
expectedFacts: filterIsInstance is `public inline fun <reified R> Flow<*>.filterIsInstance(): Flow<R> = filter { it is R } as Flow<R>` — it is inline with a reified R so the `it is R` check works at runtime; there is also a non-reified overload taking a KClass<R> in the same file
probes.author: kotlin-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'reified R> Flow<\*>.filterIsInstance' flow/operators/Transform.kt -> Transform.kt:32 (`public inline fun <reified R> Flow<*>.filterIsInstance(): Flow<R> = filter { it is R } as Flow<R>`). A second non-reified overload `filterIsInstance(klass: KClass<R>)` at Transform.kt:37. HARD: the gold is a one-line inline+reified extension function (no block body) on `Flow<*>`; the behaviour (`it is R`) is only meaningful because of `reified`, an indirection that token-level search keyed on 'instances of type' must reason about, and the KClass overload is a near-duplicate distractor.

probes.query: When I call MutableStateFlow(initialValue), what concrete class backs the returned object, and where does the actual `value` storage live?
expectedFacts: The `MutableStateFlow(value)` factory function returns `StateFlowImpl(value ?: NULL)`, and StateFlowImpl stores the state in an atomic `_state` field, boxing null as the NULL sentinel
probes.author: kotlin-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'public fun <T> MutableStateFlow' flow/StateFlow.kt -> StateFlow.kt:187 (`= StateFlowImpl(value ?: NULL)`). `private class StateFlowImpl<T>(` at StateFlow.kt:313; `private val _state = atomic(initialState)` at StateFlow.kt:316. Flow: public interface MutableStateFlow (StateFlow.kt:158) -> factory fun (187) -> private impl class (313). All within StateFlow.kt — symbol chain from public API to concrete backing.

probes.query: When a coroutine launched with `launch` fails with an uncaught exception, trace how that exception reaches a CoroutineExceptionHandler installed in the context.
expectedFacts: AbstractCoroutine.handleOnCompletionException calls the top-level handleCoroutineException(context, exception), which looks up context[CoroutineExceptionHandler] and invokes its handleException; if no handler is present (or it throws) it falls back to handleUncaughtCoroutineException
probes.author: kotlin-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'public fun handleCoroutineException' CoroutineExceptionHandler.kt -> CoroutineExceptionHandler.kt:18; body looks up `context[CoroutineExceptionHandler]?.let { it.handleException(...) ; return }` then falls back to handleUncaughtCoroutineException (lines 18-32). Caller: AbstractCoroutine.kt:115-117 `handleOnCompletionException(exception) { handleCoroutineException(context, exception) }`. Standalone coroutines from launch are AbstractCoroutine subclasses. HARD: the dispatch is via a CoroutineContext.Element key lookup (context[CoroutineExceptionHandler]) plus a global fallback — not a direct call edge; spans two files and a context-keyed indirection.

probes.query: What exactly happens when the block passed to withTimeout runs longer than the deadline, and what happens if the timeout value is zero or negative?
expectedFacts: If the block exceeds the deadline it is cancelled with a TimeoutCancellationException; if timeMillis is <= 0 withTimeout throws TimeoutCancellationException("Timed out immediately") and the block is never executed
probes.author: kotlin-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'public suspend fun <T> withTimeout(timeMillis' Timeout.kt -> Timeout.kt:23. Body: `if (timeMillis <= 0L) throw TimeoutCancellationException("Timed out immediately")` then setupTimeout(TimeoutCoroutine(...)). Doc (Timeout.kt:34-39) states block is cancelled with TimeoutCancellationException on timeout; non-positive timeout happens immediately and block is not executed. A Duration overload exists at Timeout.kt:137. Behavioral: the answer is the guard + cancellation semantics, not just the signature.

probes.query: If I set MutableStateFlow.value to something equal to the current value, do collectors get notified? Find where that decision is made.
expectedFacts: No — StateFlow conflates equal values: StateFlowImpl.updateState returns early with `if (oldState == newState) return true` so setting a value equal (by Any.equals) to the current one does not change state or notify collectors
probes.author: kotlin-author
probes.notes: grep -n 'private fun updateState' flow/StateFlow.kt -> StateFlow.kt:326; line 'if (oldState == newState) return true' at StateFlow.kt:332 (comment: "Don't do anything if value is not changing"). The `value` setter (StateFlow.kt:321) calls `updateState(null, value ?: NULL)`. Interface doc at StateFlow.kt:148 confirms conflation via Any.equals. Behavioral: the equals-conflation is a branch inside updateState, reached only by following the setter.

probes.query: Find where kotlinx.coroutines schedules coroutines onto JDK 21 virtual threads (Project Loom), e.g. via Thread.ofVirtual or startVirtualThread.
probes.author: kotlin-author
probes.notes: Verified ABSENT: grep -rin --include='*.kt' -e 'ofVirtual' -e 'VirtualThread' -e 'startVirtualThread' across the entire kotlin repo root -> 0 results. kotlinx.coroutines uses its own dispatchers/event-loop/scheduler model, not JDK Loom virtual threads.
